Answer: B
Reason: The frontal chest X-ray demonstrates a widened anterior mediastinum with loss of the normal retrosternal clear space on the lateral view, confirming an anterior location. The presence of bilateral pleural effusions (blunted costophrenic angles) in a patient with myasthenia gravis is highly suggestive of invasive thymic carcinoma with pleural metastases.
